cf.title: doc: Fix description of relative extension "directory" setting

input.subject: [PATCH] doc: Fix description of relative extension "directory" setting

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The patches change documentation and one GUC description string so that they match the code and the TAP test already shipped in 18, and message #1 gives a reproducible case. The remaining open points are the backpatch to 18 and 19, which no committer has agreed to yet, and the wording of 0003, which is not shown.

brief.title: Fix docs for relative extension directory and $system in extension_control_path
brief.problem: Since Postgres 18 (commit 81eaaa2c41d), the docs say a relative control file "directory" is resolved against the control file's directory. The code resolves it against the parent of the "extension" directory, that is SHAREDIR or the extension_control_path element. The docs also say an element that starts with $system is expanded, but only an exact "$system" is, which misleads extension authors and administrators.
brief.proposed_design: 0001 restores the pre-18 wording of "directory" in extend.sgml, extended to cover extension_control_path, and notes in config.sgml that "directory" can move script files elsewhere. 0002 says an element must be exactly $system and gets no "extension" suffix. 0003 changes the extension_control_path long description in guc_parameters.dat to match, on master only.
user_visible_surface: Docs: description of the "directory" control file parameter in extend.sgml.
Docs: description of extension_control_path in config.sgml, covering "directory" and $system.
GUC long_desc text of extension_control_path, a translatable string, master only.
author_claims: The 18 docs do not match the code; a repro shows scripts load from the base directory.
The TAP test in src/test/modules/test_extensions expects the base directory behavior.
The base directory rule keeps the "directory = 'extension/foo'" MODULEDIR convention working.
0001 and 0002 apply cleanly to REL_19_STABLE and REL_18_STABLE and should be backpatched to 18.
"$system/foo" makes CREATE EXTENSION fail, while pg_available_extensions silently skips the element.
brief.thread_state: Reviewer Matheus Alcantara (who wrote 0002) and Chao Li both say v4 looks good, and Matheus plans to mark it Ready for Committer. The author's idea of a check hook for invalid elements was moved to a separate thread.
unclear: No committer has replied, so the backpatch to 18 and 19 has no committer agreement yet.
The proposal does not say why 0002 documents the exact-match $system behavior instead of fixing the code to expand it as a prefix.
The visible text of 0003 is not shown, so reviewers cannot check the new long_desc wording.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: 0001 changes the documented rule that extension authors follow for the "directory" control file parameter; the behavior stays the same.

touch_points.label: new GUC
touch_points.reason: No new GUC, but 0002 and 0003 change the documented description and long_desc of the existing extension_control_path.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: 0001 and 0002 ask for a backpatch to 18; 0003 changes a translatable string and stays on master.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does a committer agree to backpatch 0001 and 0002 to REL_18_STABLE and REL_19_STABLE?
What is the new long_desc text in 0003, and does it match the config.sgml wording from 0001?
Should the docs for 18 also say that pg_available_extensions silently skips an element like "$system/foo" while CREATE EXTENSION fails?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the extension loading code and extension_control_path would have to confirm the wording and the backpatch; none has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: Small: the committer signs for the accuracy of two documentation paragraphs in 18, 19 and master, and one translatable GUC string on master.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted revisions up to v4 within about a week in response to review, and moved the check hook idea to a separate thread.

priority.reason: The patches are a few kilobytes of documentation that correct text contradicted by the code and by the repro in message #1. Two reviewers say v4 looks good; the audience is extension authors and administrators who set "directory" or extension_control_path.

provisional_note: The 0003 text and the code of get_extension_control_directories() were not read, so the exact-match $system claim and the new long_desc wording rest on the commit messages. The function quoted in message #2 supports the 0001 claim.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
Reverted commit(s): Read extension script files in text not binary mode.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert commit 924e03917 in favor of adding code to convert \r\n to \n
explicitly, on Windows only.  The idea of letting text mode do the
work fails for a couple of reasons:

* Per Microsoft documentation, text mode also causes control-Z to be
interpreted as end-of-file.  While it may be unlikely that extension
scripts contain control-Z, we've historically allowed it, and breaking
the case doesn't seem wise.

* Apparently, on some Windows configurations, "r" mode is interpreted
as binary not text mode.  We could force it with "rt" but that would
be inconsistent with our code elsewhere, and it would still require
Windows-specific coding.

Thanks to Alexander Lakhin for investigation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Configurable location for extension .control files
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a setting (extension_directory in the 2015 patch) so the server looks for extension .control and script files outside SHAREDIR/extension. The goal was to install extensions on systems where SHAREDIR is read-only and to test extensions against an existing installation, with superusers able to change the path at run time.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected in 2013 that a run-time adjustable extension path raises security concerns. In 2015 Heikki Linnakangas questioned the purpose of the patch and noted that extensions also need dynamic_library_path, and that timezone and tsearch data live in the same directory. For the stated goal of testing, he proposed that pgxs create a temporary installation for "make check" instead.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
In summary, the
goal is to make "make check" to work for extensions, and the way to do
that is to teach pgxs to create a temporary installation.

precedents_retrieved.title: Document creating an extension in replication setup
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds documentation on how to set up extensions in a physical replication setup: shared_preload_libraries and related settings must be configured on primary and standbys, while CREATE EXTENSION runs only on the primary and is replicated. Version 3 moved the text to high-availability.sgml and spoke of modules in general.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Julien Rouhaud's review of v3 found the wording confusing and partly wrong, and the visible messages show no later version. He said the text does not make clear that a preloaded library is needed on a standby only if it should be enabled there, including after promotion. He also said the text wrongly ties the need for preloading to whether the module exposes SQL functions.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The need for preloading is entirely orthogonal
to SQL functions in the extension, especially since this is implying SQL
function over C-code.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add control-C support for some psql meta-commands
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets control-C cancel the password prompt in psql's \password by passing psql's SIGINT longjmp target and enable flag down through simple_prompt() to pg_get_line_append(). The author planned to use the same mechanism for \prompt and \connect later.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Tom Lane's review comments were addressed in v2 and v3, and the last message posts v3 on the day the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert exporting of internal GUC variable "data_directory".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert exporting of internal GUC variable "data_directory".
Reverted commit(s): Use GUC lexer for recovery.conf parsing.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This undoes a poorly-thought-out choice in commit 970a18687f9b3058, namely
to export guc.c's internal variable data_directory.  The authoritative
variable so far as C code is concerned is DataDir; there is no reason for
anything except specific bits of GUC code to look at the GUC variable.

After yesterday's commits fixing the fsync-on-restart patch, the only
remaining misuse of data_directory was in AlterSystemSetConfigFile(),
which would be much better off just using a relative path anyhow: it's
less code and it doesn't break if the DBA moves the data directory of a
running system, which is a case we've taken some pains over in the past.

This is mostly cosmetic, so no need for a back-patch (and I'd be hesitant
to remove a global variable in stable branches anyway).

precedents_retrieved.title: logical replication access control
precedents_retrieved.summary: A patch set to let ordinary users with explicit privileges manage logical replication instead of requiring superuser or replication roles. It added a PUBLICATION privilege on tables, a USAGE privilege on publications, a CREATE SUBSCRIPTION privilege on databases, privilege checks in apply workers, and normal database entries in pg_hba.conf for logical replication.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Stephen Frost argued that publishing a table should be an owner right rather than a grantable privilege, and the author dropped the PUBLICATION privilege in favor of owner rights. The author withdrew the USAGE privilege on publications because of issues raised in the thread. The author then returned the rest because a CREATE SUBSCRIPTION privilege granted on a database could be assigned by a database owner who may not be privileged enough to make that decision. Two parts were committed: the publication owner fix and the pg_hba.conf change.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
One new concern I just thought about is that having GRANT whatever ON
DATABASE would allow a database owner to assign these privileges, but a
database owner is not necessarily someone highly privileged to make this
decision.

precedents_retrieved.title: A separate table level option to control compression
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a table storage option, compress_tuple_target, that sets the tuple length at which inline compression starts, separate from toast_tuple_target. A table can then compress tuples shorter than the toast threshold without moving them out of line.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier found that the existing code ignores a toast_tuple_target lower than the compile-time TOAST_TUPLE_THRESHOLD, and the patch changes that behaviour as a side effect. He opened a separate thread to decide whether this is a bug and said that question must be settled first, since otherwise this patch is wrong and needs rework. The feature freeze was two days away, so he marked the entry returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If we don't use the other patch, then what's proposed on this
thread is actually wrong and should be reworked.

precedents_retrieved.title: Checkpoint extension hook
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Heikki Linnakangas, Andres Freund
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an rm_checkpoint() callback to the custom resource manager (rmgr) interface, so extensions can run code during CheckPointGuts(). Later versions add a phase argument, with calls before and after CheckPointBuffers(), and a pg_stat_statements patch shows its use.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas judged the hook unfinished: no working, documented example or table AM use case showed that the v3 design was good enough, and the pg_stat_statements patch was a POC based on v2. Heikki Linnakangas found that the pg_stat_statements patch WAL-logs every pgss_store() call and fails on a standby. He argued that checkpoint actions do not belong in the rmgr interface, which is about WAL replay, and asked for an independent hook. Andres Freund earlier objected to running extension code inside CheckPointGuts() with no rules on what is legal there.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
My basic position is not that this patch is a bad idea, but that it
isn't really finished.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support % wildcard in extension upgrade scripts
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let an extension ship an update script with % as the old version, such as postgis--%--3.2.0.sql, which matches any installed version when no explicit update path exists. Later versions made this opt-in with a wildcard_upgrades switch in the .control file.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The last patch failed the extension regression test and no rebase followed, so Daniel Gustafsson marked it returned with feedback. Robert Haas said the real problem was no consensus on a design, since Tom Lane opposed any design that solves the authors' problem. Quoted text from Tom Lane says a wildcard script makes authors promise correct behaviour from any old version, including downgrades, which authors will not do.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The fact that consensus is that far away and no patch that applies exist seems to me to indicate that a new CF entry is a better option than pushing forward.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fast path for empty relids in check_outerjoin_delay()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an early return to check_outerjoin_delay() when the given relids are empty, the same exit already taken when there are no special joins. The author presented it as a readability change with no expected performance gain.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut argued that more special cases and fast paths make the code harder to read and maintain. Tom Lane agreed the patch should be rejected: it is unlikely to help performance, does not improve readability, and empty relids reach the function only from check_equivalence_delay. Tom suggested a larger refactoring of check_outerjoin_delay and the SpecialJoinInfo structures, and closed the entry when no follow-on patch came by the end of the commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Anyway, I concur with Peter that the patch you've presented should
probably be rejected: I doubt it's a win performance-wise and I don't
see that it adds anything to readability either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add TAP test to automate the equivalent of check_guc"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add TAP test to automate the equivalent of check_guc"
Reverted commit(s): Add TAP test to automate the equivalent of check_guc
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b0a55f4, to remove for now the TAP test that did the
equivalent of check_guc.  The test has been using pg_config --sharedir
to find the location of postgresql.conf.sample.  While the buildfarm and
normal build environments rather liked that, this proves to be an issue
for Debian where pg_config is patched to not be relocatable, causing the
test to fail.

Rather than relying on pg_config, we'd better find the sample file based
on its location from the source directory.  However, this is also an
issue as a TAP test only offers the build directory as of TESTDIR in the
environment context, so this would fail with VPATH builds.  Perhaps the
source path could be provided additionally when running the TAP tests.
Or perhaps we may be able to get away by just switching to a SQL
approach, by using PG_ABS_SRCDIR but this is going to require some extra
loops to get the sample file from the correct path in src/backend/.  In
any case, this needs more thoughts, so just revert the test case until
something better is done about this relocation problem.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no proposal about the same or a similar idea. The thread points to only one earlier discussion: message #6 links an extension_control_path bug about empty path elements, which is a separate code issue and was not rejected. This docs fix gives no prior rejection reason to apply.

The patch changes no behavior. It brings the 18 docs in line with what the code and the TAP test already do, so no query, script or dump behaves differently after upgrade. The 0002 choice of exact-match $system has a stated reason, because $system already names the extension directory, and the prefix form never worked. Keeping the translatable long_desc change on master only follows existing backpatch practice.

The patches change only documentation and, in 0003, the GUC long_desc string. Nothing in them touches on-disk format, WAL, replication, catalogs, the wire protocol or the extension ABI. A translatable string is a backpatch concern, and 0003 already keeps it on master only.

This is a docs-only fix plus one GUC long_desc string, and it does not change who can do what. extension_control_path and the "directory" behavior already exist. Documenting the real resolution rule and the exact-match $system rule exposes no new privilege, data, or file system access. A correct description helps administrators see where script files load from.

This is a docs-only fix that makes the text match code and tests already shipped in 18, so it adds no hot-path cost, API or new mechanism to maintain. Keeping the translatable long_desc change on master only follows the usual practice. 0002 documents the exact-match $system rule and gives its reason, a sound one, in the commit message. No committer has replied yet, so the backpatch to 18 has no committer agreement.

This is a docs-only fix that makes the documentation match existing behavior. No existing feature, extension or tool supplies correct documentation, so nothing is duplicated. The open questions, such as backpatch agreement and whether to change the $system code instead, belong to other angles.

This is a docs-only fix where the current text in 18 describes behavior the code does not have, and message #1 shows a reproducible case. Every user of the "directory" and $system settings is affected, so demand is not in question. No objection from the demand angle.
